items.text: A video has been released showing armed military forces present at a boys' school in Urmia. This school is located in the center of West Azerbaijan province. The news was reported by Iran International.

Ebrahim bin Sultan Al-Hashimi, director of media at Qatar's Foreign Ministry, stated that mediation efforts between the US and the Islamic Republic continue without interruption. The goal is to achieve progress that allows addressing the concerns of both sides. Qatar is mediating between Washington and Tehran, with messages being exchanged.
The deputy supervisor of public places at Tehran's police announced that cafes on Sanayi and Iranshahr streets were closed due to these streets becoming places for cruising and street vending.

Mohammad Reza Rezaei-Kochi, head of the Parliament's Civil Commission, called for the immediate removal of excessive regulations in cargo clearance and the establishment of unified management in ports and border terminals. He emphasized that executive agencies must supply essential goods as quickly as possible. The head of the Ports and Maritime Organization stated that maritime transport and transit operations have decreased by 45 percent.

The Janfadaian Isfahan exercise was held on October 1st, featuring men in plain clothes carrying cold weapons. The exercise aimed to demonstrate public readiness and capacities. Legal experts described the open carrying of cold weapons as a show of force.

Mohsen Babaian, a prisoner arrested during the December 1404 protests, was sentenced to death by Branch 26 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court on charges of moharebeh. The sentence was issued by Judge Iman Afshari and was communicated to him yesterday. The news was reported by the HRANA news agency.
A video shows heavy traffic in a street in Mashhad due to a government gathering and the presence of Basij forces. This event took place on Tuesday. Vehicle movement in the area has been disrupted.

Prosecutors in London have accused three Iranian men of spying for the intelligence agencies of the Islamic Republic. The individuals are charged with monitoring Iran International journalists and taking photos and videos of related locations. The charges are based on the UK's National Security Act 2023.

Donald Trump suggested the possibility of Tehran's role in the FlyDubai incident. Israel prepared its fighters after the co-pilot attack but refrained from shooting down the plane after it changed course to Saudi Arabia. In the UK, a person has been arrested in connection with the planned attack on the Fairford base.

IRNA news agency reported that an explosion sound was heard from the sea side in Qeshm Island. So far, no reports of impact or damage on the island have been announced. Local sources have not provided details about the explosion.

Citizens in Iran report increasing pressure from inflation and difficulty in meeting basic living needs. Some have resorted to selling educational books to provide food for their children. Additionally, buying semi-rotten fruits has increased due to high prices.

Hosseinali Hajideligani called for the establishment of an independent deputy in the Central Bank to counter the currency war. He stated that the US has explicitly announced plans to devalue Iran's national currency. He also pointed to the need to revise the currency distribution mechanism and reduce the economy's dependence on the dollar.

Four workers died in an elevator fall accident in Royan. A street cleaner died on the Ravanser-Kermanshah route, and several workers were injured in the Dasht Palang dam project and an industrial unit in Semnan. These incidents occurred due to a lack of workplace safety.
Students are forcibly recruited into the Basij and exploited. Financial and economic problems are putting pressure on families. In some schools, war identification tags are being distributed.
Israeli fighter jets are on alert in the Flydubai incident. An attack plan on Fairford has also been mentioned. This topic was discussed in the Titrawal audio version with Niusha Saremi.

Yahya Saree, spokesperson for the Houthi armed forces, claimed that Saudi Arabia carried out 66 air and missile attacks on civilian targets in several Yemeni provinces in the past 24 hours. These attacks were conducted with F-15 and Typhoon fighter jets and armed reconnaissance aircraft. The total number of attacks since the escalation of the conflict has reached 1,642.

A staff member of the anti-plague institute in Siberia died under suspicious circumstances. About 200 people who had contact with him have been quarantined. Russian authorities have not confirmed plague infection, and the World Health Organization considers the risk of an outbreak low.

Jamal Khodarahmi and Hirsh Navgaran, citizens of Sanandaj, were sentenced to a total of five years of suspended imprisonment. Jamal Khodarahmi was also sentenced to pay a fine. The sentence was issued by the judicial authority.

Workers of North Drilling Company have reported delays in the payment of their wages and demands. Workers at the Mohammadabad CNG station have not received their salaries for five months, and workers at Marun Oil and Gas Industrial Complex No. 6 are facing three months of unpaid wages and non-payment of insurance premiums.

A citizen reported on October 6 about the scarcity of psychiatric drugs in Isfahan. These drugs are hard to find in pharmacies and are expensive even with social security insurance. They are also being sold on the black market.

Mehdi Mahdavi Azad said Sistan and Baluchestan is one of the most deprived regions in Iran. He added that the Islamic Republic views the province with a security perspective due to its Baluch and Sunni population. This security approach has intensified division and distrust in the province.

Neymar emotionally bid farewell to Lionel Messi, who is about to play his last match for Argentina's national team. He thanked Messi for his impact on football and their football relationship. Messi is set to retire from the national team after a friendly match against Benin.

Abdolnaser Hemmati, the governor of the Central Bank, announced that the monthly growth of liquidity in the country has declined. He stated that there are plans to control inflation and currency fluctuations. Hemmati emphasized that the Central Bank understands the economic conditions and has made plans.

The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps issued a statement warning that any new military action against Iran will be met with a devastating response. The statement referenced past conflicts and Iran's control over the Strait of Hormuz. It also emphasized that the resistance will continue until the liberation of Jerusalem and the destruction of Israel.

The audio version of the program 24 with Fardad Farahzad has been released. The program discusses the Islamic Republic's involvement in the plan to attack the Fairford airbase. This program was broadcast on Iran International.

Cristiano Ronaldo stated that he decided to leave the Portugal national team camp after the coach did not fulfill their agreement. He emphasized that he is still ready to participate in the national team. Ronaldo also explained his support for the current coach and details about his playing schedule.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, told reporters on Tuesday, 14 Mehr, at the White House that millions of barrels of oil have been transferred through the Strait of Hormuz in recent days, and oil transfer levels now sometimes exceed pre-war levels.

There has been an unprecedented increase in armed clashes in Sistan and Baluchestan. This issue was discussed in the program Cheshmandaz with Mehdi Mahdavi Azad. The full episode is available on YouTube.

Abdolnaser Hemmati, the governor of the Central Bank, said that the American officials' promise of the collapse of Iran's economy will not come true. He understands the economic pressures on the people and the government is trying to reduce problems during the economic war.

British police have arrested the seventh suspect linked to a suspected Tehran-backed plot to attack an airbase. The suspect is a 22-year-old British national detained in London. After receiving intelligence reports, the Pentagon withdrew a fleet of bombers from the RAF Fairford base.

Donald Trump said the US Navy has imposed one of the most effective and impenetrable blockades in history against Iran, and no ship can pass through it. He added that if a ship attempts to pass and carries oil, its cabin or rudder will be targeted, and if it has no oil, it will be sunk. Trump also said the Strait of Hormuz is now under US control and belongs to the US Navy.

Donald Trump, the US President, in a speech in Maryland, called the Islamic Republic "evil and a bully in the Middle East" and stated that the Iranian government "is no longer much of a bully." He emphasized that the US Navy ensures Tehran will never acquire nuclear weapons, and this issue "is practically certain." Trump also claimed that Iran's air and naval forces have been destroyed, with 159 of their ships now at the bottom of the sea.

New reports have emerged about the possibility of a nuclear war during the Yom Kippur War. Moshe Dayan proposed using nuclear weapons to intimidate enemies. This proposal was opposed by ministers and completely rejected by Golda Meir.

Morad Vaisi, a senior analyst at Iran International, stated that executions in the Islamic Republic are ineffective and even increase public anger. He said these executions have a boomerang effect and make society more explosive. Vaisi described the government as foolish for thinking people would be intimidated by the executions.

Scott Bassett, the US Treasury Secretary, commented on Iran's new oil minister on social media. He stated that Iran has not loaded any crude oil onto a ship since August 25. He questioned what the new oil minister is supposed to manage.

Morad Vaisi stated that the behavior of revolutionary people and the opposition is partly determined by the ruling government. He added that the Islamic Republic's criminal suppression methods have angered the people more. This plays a role in the process of the government's overthrow.

Amin Nasser, CEO of Aramco, stated that global commercial oil reserves have fallen below six billion barrels, with most of it inaccessible. The International Energy Agency plans to release 100 million barrels of oil, but supplying it is challenging. Industry leaders expect market disruption to continue until next year.

Despite the return of Middle East oil flow to pre-war conditions, the oil market remains unstable. Producers are seeking new pipelines. China has increased its contracts with Iraq and Qatar, putting heavy financial pressure on Iran.

Kambiz Tavana stated that despite the increase in energy exports and transfers, maritime security in the Strait of Hormuz has not returned to pre-conflict conditions. Attacks continue and ships require military escort. One method of cargo transfer is ship-to-ship after passing through the Strait of Hormuz.

Mohammad Qaedi stated that reaching Sanaa in the short term is not feasible but can be a long-term strategic goal. Stabilizing government forces in coastal areas and moving towards Al Hudaydah can increase pressure on the Houthis. Controlling strategic areas around Bab al-Mandab reduces but does not eliminate the threat to international shipping.

JD Vance stated that Iran must significantly reduce its nuclear enrichment capacity to meet US demands. He emphasized that if Iran does not want nuclear weapons, it should not produce highly enriched fuel. The US remains ready for an agreement but demands specific nuclear concessions.

Donald Trump said that the US military capability is expanding unprecedentedly and 17 new factories, including weapons factories, have been built. He described Iran's economic situation as 'terrible' and noted the recent resignation of Iran's oil minister. Trump also said that oil tanker traffic in the Strait of Hormuz has reached pre-war levels.

Germany's domestic intelligence agency says the Islamic Republic is seeking advanced missile technologies from Germany. Iran's missile system technology program includes ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, and drones. Iran is also pursuing CNC machines, vacuum pumps, and small explosion-proof engines made in Germany.

Satellite images show significant activity has resumed at the Minzadehi site in northeast Tehran. This site is linked to nuclear weapons development and underwent extensive cleanup after an Israeli attack in March. The Israeli army targeted the site and stated that Iranian nuclear scientists had been visiting it before the attack.

New satellite images show increased activity at the mine-clearing facility in northeast Tehran after the Israeli attack in March. Israel and the Institute for Science and International Security consider this facility linked to Iran's nuclear weapons efforts. This report was published by the Jerusalem Post.

Amir Hamidi stated that Reza Pahlavi's stance on the Islamic Republic's presence in Latin America links the Iran issue to the national security of regional countries. He added that the joint statement by the US and nine other countries regarding the Islamic Republic's activities could lead to judicial and police cooperation. The Islamic Republic's model in this region is multilayered, involving the Quds Force, Hezbollah, and front companies.

The Aden Security Media Office announced that two missiles were fired by the Houthis at Aden International Airport. No reports of human casualties have been released. This airport is the main gateway for international communications for parts of Yemen outside Houthi control.

Marco Rubio called on Russia to provide more information about the death of a plague research lab worker in Siberia. The WHO Secretary-General confirmed the follow-up on the incident and requested more details. Russian officials stated that no dangerous pathogens were identified.

The Associated Press, citing a US official, reported that RAF Fairford base in England faced threats linked to the Iranian regime. The Trump administration believes the aim of these threats was to kill US forces and destroy American aircraft. The official, who spoke on condition of anonymity, did not provide details about the nature of the possible attack.

The UN Secretary-General, during his visit to Pakistan, called on Iran and the US to pursue diplomacy. He praised Islamabad's efforts for peace and stability. He also condemned the October 7 Hamas attack and Israeli actions in Gaza.

JD Vance stated that the US is still ready to reach an agreement with Tehran but demands specific nuclear concessions. He emphasized that words will not be exchanged for actions. Washington also does not know who makes decisions in Tehran.

South Korea has sent over 176,000 tons of petroleum products to Russia in two months. Ukraine considers this action contrary to Seoul's sanction policy and says it reduces fuel shortages caused by its attacks on Russian refineries. South Korea has emphasized enforcing export restrictions without explaining the shipments.

Hossein Shariatmadari suggested that the seven-month closure of the parliament might have been indirectly imposed on the system. He interpreted the appointment of Qalibaf as head of the negotiation team as equivalent to the parliament's closure. Shariatmadari also pointed out the contradiction in Qalibaf's role in the negotiation team.

Yashar Soltani published documents indicating that Mojtaba Zolnouri is involved in illegal excavation for historical artifacts and treasure. He also stated that the spokesperson of the Stability Front's son-in-law is one of the oil recipients. Earlier, the head of the archaeology institute at Tehran University mentioned the presence of a parliament member in treasure hunting activities.

Alireza Namvar Haghighi said Iran must make significant concessions, including uranium transfer and suspension of enrichment, to reach an agreement with the US. He also emphasized that Iran has lost the ability to make decisions and build consensus. If the agreement is not accepted, a full-scale conflict or prolonged war may occur.

The World Health Organization is investigating the death of an employee at the Anti-Plague Research Institute in Irkutsk, Russia. There are reports of his possible infection with pneumonic plague. Russian officials have denied any cases of plague in the region.

A US official told the Associated Press that the threat against RAF Fairford in Britain, aimed at killing US forces and destroying US military aircraft, was linked to the Islamic Republic. Meanwhile, British police arrested a seventh suspect in the case.

Yemeni government forces, supported by Saudi airstrikes, have retaken parts of the coasts around the Bab al-Mandab Strait from the Houthis. They advanced close to the city of Mocha. This operation aims to reclaim areas that the Houthis had captured last month.

Reza Goharzad said the rapid reconstruction of nuclear sites indicates that the Islamic Republic is seeking to revive its nuclear capability. He added that these actions could increase the likelihood of another Israeli attack on Iran. He also emphasized that the Islamic Republic, with a possible exit from the NPT, aims to repeat North Korea's pattern.

The Israeli Prime Minister said Hamas, despite being severely weakened, might attempt an attack on Israel before the elections. He emphasized that the Israeli army is prepared to confront any attack. Netanyahu promised a harsh response to any aggression.

The housing crisis in Spain has become a major challenge for Pedro Sánchez's government. The government has approved a new plan to address this crisis. Labor unions have announced the possibility of a general strike.

Lionel Messi scored in his final national team match against Benin, bringing his total international goals to 126. The friendly match ended with Argentina winning 3-0, and Messi played the full 90 minutes. After the game, a ceremony with 85,000 spectators took place, and Messi gave an emotional speech.

Pegah Bani-Hashemi stated that the Islamic Republic violates international and domestic laws in the execution process. She pointed to prisoners being denied access to lawyers and reports of torture. Bani-Hashemi emphasized the need for a national consensus against executions.

Najmeh Amini, a 23-year-old woman, has been sentenced to death by the Sixth Branch of the Criminal Court One of Khorasan Razavi for blasphemy and insulting the Imams in cyberspace. She previously announced the death sentence in an audio file from Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad. Fars News Agency stated that no final verdict has been issued yet and the court of appeals has not commented on the case.
Ali Shirazi said that Hossein Shariatmadari's criticisms of Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf reflect the Stability Front's concern about a possible secret agreement between Ghalibaf and the United States.

On the third anniversary of the October 7 attacks, the Australian Prime Minister emphasized combating anti-Semitism and disarming Hamas. Hundreds gathered at Bondi Beach in Sydney to pay tribute to the victims. Iran International's reporter provided more details.

On the third anniversary of Hamas's October 7 attack on Israel, CCTV footage shows parts of the attack. The footage includes Hamas vehicles and forces attacking a music festival and killing in residential areas. The report was prepared by Abtin Yazdanpanah for Iran International.

The French Student Union reported 450,000 people protesting against school conditions and budget cuts. The Ministry of the Interior stated the number of protesters as 256,000. Approximately 1,800 high schools have been closed, shut down, or disrupted during the protests.

A group of political activists and Iranians living in Germany gathered in Hanover and Hamburg. They protested the execution of Alireza Sepahi and Alireza Raeisi and demanded the release of political prisoners. Participants also expressed their support for Reza Pahlavi and commemorated the popular uprisings in Iran.

Security forces transferred Alireza Raeisi's father with a blindfold for burial after his execution, without revealing the exact burial location. The burial took place in a desert area near Isfahan, and the family remains unaware of the precise grave site. Security officials have stated that the burial location will be announced later.

The head of the Thalassemia Association announced that each thalassemia patient now has to spend over 100 million tomans monthly for treatment. The cost of some medicines has increased more than 600 times after the removal of preferential currency rates. Additionally, pharmacy claims have not been paid for over 10 months and insurance companies are delayed in covering the increased drug prices.

Reuters reported that at least 12 attacks on oil tankers and gas carriers were recorded in the Strait of Hormuz last week. The US-led Maritime Information Center stated that in addition to attacks, drone flights and radio communications by the IRGC continued. These actions are described as an effort by the Islamic Republic to maintain pressure on passing ships.

Bahareh Aghaei, a detained lawyer in Qarchak Varamin prison, has been sentenced to 20 years in prison. The Shirin Ebadi Telegram channel stated that supporting December protesters, attending the 40th-day ceremony of Sepehr Shokri, and providing legal aid to families seeking justice are among the charges against her.

Scott Bessent, the US Treasury Secretary, sarcastically reacted on X to the resignation of Iran's Oil Minister Mohsen Paknejad, asking what the new oil minister is managing given that not a single barrel of oil has been loaded since August 25.

One of Seyed Ahmad Seyed Abdollahi's cases was closed by a suspension of prosecution order issued by the Borujen County court. The case involved charges of propaganda against the Islamic Republic system. He is serving his sentence in prison for another case.

Kamil Mohammadi, a resident of Mashhad and nephew of Narges Mohammadi, was arrested by security forces on Thursday, October 1. After his arrest, he was taken for interrogation and then transferred to the Revolutionary Court and prison in Mashhad.

Reuters reported that Hezbollah received 200 million dollars from the Islamic Republic last month to provide financial aid to families displaced by the war with Israel. Each family is to receive three thousand dollars, prioritizing those whose villages were destroyed or who cannot return. Hezbollah will announce the distribution plan in the coming days.

Iran International has obtained exclusive information about the recruitment operation of Hezbollah's Unit 910 in Iran. The identities of five members of this project, including an American cleric, and the addresses of their operational houses in Qom and Tehran have been revealed. The report was prepared by Mojtaba Pourmohsen.

The Islamic Republic provided Hezbollah Lebanon with 200 million dollars last month to assist displaced Lebanese families affected by the war with Israel. Hezbollah plans to give about three thousand dollars to each family. Priority will be given to families whose villages were destroyed or who cannot return home.
A video shows a protester in Sabzevar burning a banner with the image of Ali Khamenei. The video was received by Iran International. This event took place in Sabzevar.

Marco Rubio emphasized during his trip to Greece that Washington will not allow the Islamic Republic to obtain nuclear weapons. He also pointed to missed opportunities for agreement by the Islamic Republic. These remarks came after news about new nuclear activities in Iran.
Iran provided $200 million in cash aid to Hezbollah Lebanon last month. This aid is to be distributed among 50,000 families affected by the war in Lebanon. Each family will receive $3,000.

Manouchehr Motaki stated that free passage of ships in the Strait of Hormuz will resume once Tehran's conditions are met. These conditions include lifting the blockade and removing restrictions on civilian aviation. He also condemned attacks against the Islamic Republic.
